newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Stg/mark rally tiring, focus on support.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Stg/mark rally tiring, focus on support.

text.p: Sterling/mark continues to plod higher from last week's 2.7417 low, but its rally is becoming laboured and a dip to support looks likely, chartists said.
The pound pushed through 2.78 marks on Tuesday but a string of hurdles is seen above there, making the upside going tough.

"Upside risk would only materialize above 2.7890 -- that looks out of reach. I favour renewed weakness and watch closely the very short-term support area at 2.7715/30," said Dominique Corombelle, technical analyst at Generale Bank in Brussels.
The pound was quoted at 2.7815/25 marks at 0719 GMT, up from 2.7715/25 in late Europe on Tuesday.
A break of the congestive support band around 2.7715-30 will open 2.7650 -- previous resistance -- and the psychological 2.76, chartists said.
Early upside resistance appears around 2.7850 marks, a 66.6 percent retracement of sterling's recent drop from around 2.8081 to 2.7403, analysts said.
Cable, meantime, is consolidating, but analysts said the bias is to the downside.
"It keeps threatening to break back down and attack the medium-term lows. There is a window today to do that," said Eddie Matts, director at Capital Management UK.
"To do that today, it needs to clear $1.6280 -- which is hourly trend support -- and until then should hold below $1.6340-60, or else it's going to see more consolidation below $1.6450," he said.
Sterling stood at $1.6322/32 at 0849 GMT compared to late yesterday's European level of $1.6312/22.
RSI - 14 day: Stg/mark: 51 pct, Stg/dollar: 49 pct
